newsitem.title: USA: Experimental U.S. CPI index unchanged in May.
newsitem.headline: Experimental U.S. CPI index unchanged in May.

text.p: The Labour Department said on Tuesday its experimental geometric mean Consumer Price Index was unchanged in May after a 0.1 percent rise in April.
Excluding the volatile food and energy sectors, the measure fell 0.1 percent after a 0.3 percent rise in April.
The Labour Department releases two experimental CPI versions as part of its monthly reading on different ways of measuring inflation in the United States.
Labour Department data released a week ago showed that the traditional version of the CPI rose 0.1 percent in May. Excluding the volatile food and energy sectors, it showed a 0.2 percent increase.

"This is exactly what you should expect," said Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc. "The geometric means (used for the experimental CPI) will always be less than the arithmetic means that are used to put together the regular CPI. That's a mathematical certainty."
The experimental index uses two formula bases: the geometric formula differs from the official current method because it takes into account consumers' tendency to substitute among similar items.
"The way the current index is constructed, they assume people don't make substitutions in their buying patterns," said Joshua Feinman, vice president and global market economist at Bankers Trust.

"The experimental CPI will try on a limited basis to mimic a certain kind of substitution that consumers would make," he said. "They (department officials) don't actually go out and speak to consumers. They calculate the CPI as if consumers went out and substituted goods."
Over the last 12 months, the experimental CPI has been running two or three tenths of a percentage point lower on an annual basis than the regular CPI, the economist said.
The other experimental version, known as the Laspeyres formula, uses the same mathematical base as the current CPI but adds a technical adjustment to make it comparable to the geometric mean index.

The department reported that the Laspeyres test CPI fell 0.1 percent in May after a 0.2 percent rise in April. Without the food and energy components, it remained unchanged in May after a 0.2 percent increase in April.
